Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, I’m following up with a concise ask from Mediwave’s procurement team so we can move the order form and exhibit language forward into your procurement queue.

Quick summary of what we need from Redwood to align with Mediwave’s internal risk banding:
- A defined service credit schedule that maps percentage of monthly uptime degradation to credit percentage (example attached: ServiceCreditSchedule_v2.xlsx).
- Wording for an "Order Form Exhibit: Availability & Credits" (draft attached: OrderForm_Exhibit_SLA_v1.docx) that can live as an exhibit to the order form rather than amending the MSA.
- Confirmation whether uptime calculations exclude scheduled maintenance windows and regional failover time (we typically exclude scheduled maintenance, but Mediwave wants explicit callouts).

For timeline: Mediwave indicated they need a doc suitable for internal review by COB Monday PT to avoid delaying their procurement meeting on Tuesday. Can we target a short confirmation + updated exhibit by end of day Monday?

I’ve attached the MSA with Mediwave’s redlines for context (MediWave_MSA_Redlines_20260529.pdf). Ben and Lauren are looped for pricing/order form signoff.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood provides an updated order form exhibit and a service credit schedule that maps to the percentages in the attached spreadsheet.
2) Ben confirms any required billing/crediting operational notes.
3) Lauren confirms wording is acceptable for order form placement (exhibit vs addendum).

Appreciate quick turnaround — I know this is tight.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the redlines. A few clarifying questions from our side before we finalize internal review:

1) In the attached service credit schedule (v2) you show a 2-hour tolerance window per month before credits start. Is that a fixed buffer or relative to expected uptime%? Mediwave needs the definition explicitly called out.
2) For regional failover: if Redwood fails over from us-west to us-east for a customer-specific private deployment, how is uptime measured? We need to understand whether that counts as degraded availability or continuous availability for the tenant.
3) Can you confirm the point of contact and process for applying credits (ticket, timeline, and whether credits are pro-rated against the next invoice)?

We can push for the Monday review if we get a brief response on these points and updated exhibit language that is standalone (we prefer exhibit to reduce MSA churn).

—Emily Park

Jordan / Markus —

Operational notes from my side:
- The 2-hour tolerance currently behaves as a monthly aggregate buffer. We can call it a "monthly tolerance window" in the exhibit. Credits kick in after the monthly tolerance is exceeded.
- For private/dedicated deployments: failover between regions will be treated as continuous availability so long as service remains reachable via the designated endpoints; if client-initiated failover or network-level routing change causes interruption, that will be excluded. We should add a short definition of "regional failover" with examples.
- Credit application flow: customer opens a support ticket using the "Billing & Credits" template. Once validated by Ops (usually within 5 business days), credits are applied to the next invoice as an account-level credit. We can include a 45-day window for customer to request credit after incident.

I drafted suggested bullet language and added it to the OrderForm_Exhibit_SLA_v1.docx (see comments). If legal approves the plain-language bullets, we can send back to Mediwave before EOD Monday.

Ben Carter

Emily —

Thanks for the questions and for flagging procurement timing. Jordan/Bens' bullets look fine from a contract perspective; a few firming edits we propose below so Mediwave can plug them into procurement: 

1) Monthly Tolerance Window: "Customer will receive Service Credits only for unplanned availability degradations that exceed an aggregate of two (2) hours within a single calendar month (the 'Monthly Tolerance Window'). Scheduled maintenance and customer-requested downtime are excluded from this measurement."

2) Regional Failover: "For Dedicated or Private deployments, an automatic routing or infrastructure failover performed by Redwood that does not require any customer action will not be treated as an availability failure for purposes of Service Credits if end-to-end connectivity to the tenant's endpoint is preserved. Customer-initiated failover scenarios or changes to customer-managed networking that result in interruption shall be excluded."

3) Credit Issuance Process: "To request Service Credits, Customer must submit a ticket using the 'Billing & Credits' template within forty-five (45) days of the incident. Redwood will validate the incident within five (5) business days following ticket receipt and, if validated, will apply a credit to the next invoice within the subsequent billing cycle. "

We can produce a redline of OrderForm_Exhibit_SLA_v1.docx showing the exact insertions; I've attached a redlined PDF for you to share with procurement. If this language meets Mediwave's needs, Jordan — please confirm and I'll produce a clean exhibit for insertion into the order form and a separate PDF for procurement review.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
